conclusion: Two concurrent workers reduced throughput on this GPU under the fixed four-CPU aggregate quota, including when specialized quotient kernels remained enabled. Keep one worker per GPU by default.
interpretation: The first two comparisons selected the generic GPU quotient interpreter because specialization normally requires a 4 GiB context allowance. Restoring the full 7 GiB managed budget did not restore specialized kernels. The final isolated variant retained specialization under a freshly calibrated 224 MiB context allowance and a 64 MiB private-backing bound, with synchronized context enforcement.
source_changes: Only isolated source snapshots changed for the experiment.
Validated controller-owned exclusive device lease passed to assigned worker services.
Lower context allowance only after transferred lease validation.
Specialized variant additionally records validated lease state, permits calibrated specialization, caps private backing, and enforces the context allowance.
validation: Every root-only verification, selected wallet verification, recursive node verification, and journal replay passed on CPU.
Every recursive proof reported all 16 proving stages on OpenCL.
Measured GPU processes demonstrably overlapped; simultaneous kernel execution was not profiled.
No new worker or fleet RAM-limit/OOM events and no swap.
Source, control, input, support, binary, and proof manifests validated.
All three patches reconstruct their exact measured source changes.
Two focused exclusive lease lifetime/exclusion and invalid-descriptor tests passed on the unchanged lease module.

Final reporter, repeat helper, and reproduction instructions retained in each reporting/ directory; specialized repeat helper passed preparation-only validation without launching GPU work or copying proof outputs.
